enrollment_evidence_quote: Go ahead and click Sign... and that's it, every signature is done. Congratulations!

program_and_guarantee_limits.evidence_quote: Debt resolution is not a loan, is not credit counseling, and is not a credit repair program. FDR cannot guarantee that your creditors will agree to resolve your debts, resolve your debts for a specific amount, or resolve your debts within a certain time.

financial_distress_suitability.evidence_quote: Debt resolution is suitable only for persons who are in financial distress and unable to pay or continue to pay their minimum monthly payments without hardship.

creditworthiness_impact.evidence_quote: The use of a debt resolution program will adversely affect your creditworthiness, as creditors report the status of your enrolled debts to credit bureaus.

collections_and_lawsuits_risk.evidence_quote: Your creditors may subject you to collections or lawsuits, charge you fees, assess penalties, and raise your rates for not making payments on your enrolled debts.

deposit_commitment_and_bankruptcy_altern.evidence_quote: Your success depends on your ability to make regular deposits into an FDIC-insured dedicated account administered by a payment processor. If you cannot make these deposits, you should consider alternatives to address your financial hardship, including bankruptcy.

dedicated_account_control.evidence_quote: You own and control the dedicated account. Funds in this account will only be used to pay settlements to your creditors, fees to the payment processor, and fees to FDR for debt resolution services provided.

performance_based_fees.evidence_quote: FDR will not earn and will not be paid its fee for settling a debt until FDR obtains a settlement agreement from a creditor, you approve that agreement, and a payment is made on that settlement.

withdrawal_rights.evidence_quote: You may withdraw from the debt resolution program at any time without penalty. If you withdraw, you are entitled to funds remaining in the dedicated account, less any fees earned by FDR or the payment processor that have not yet been paid.

tax_consequences.evidence_quote: Your creditors may report settlement savings of $600 or more to the IRS. FDR does not provide tax advice. You should consult a tax advisor to determine whether to report these savings as taxable income.
